entries.topic: No constitution; Basic Laws; the Law of Return

claims.text: Law of Return passed 5 July 1950: "Every Jew has the right to come to this country as an oleh"; 1970 amendment (§4A) extends the rights to a Jew's child and grandchild, spouse, and the spouses of child and grandchild (excluding a Jew who voluntarily converted); §4B defines a Jew as born of a Jewish mother or converted, and not a member of another religion.

Basic Law: Torah Study passed in July 2026, declaring Torah study "a fundamental value in the heritage of the Jewish people and the State of Israel"; petitions challenge it in the High Court; a companion law freezing arrests of Haredi draft evaders until 30 November 2026 was suspended by a High Court interim order. Basic Laws were meant to be adopted chapter by chapter under the 1950 Harari Resolution.

sources.label: Jewish Virtual Library, Law of Return 5710–1950 (text and amendments)
Unpacked, "Torah study and legal immunity: what are the new laws shaking Israel?", July 2026

claims.text: Election held 27 October 2026; results published 4 November; seats: Likud 27, Yashar (Eisenkot) 21, B'Yachad 12, Joint List 11, Democrats 8, Ra'am 8, Yisrael Beiteinu 7, Otzma Yehudit 7, UTJ 7, Shas 6, Religious Zionism-Zehut 6; Netanyahu-aligned bloc 53, Eisenkot-led bloc 48, Arab-led parties 19 (a record). Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate on 8 November 2026 on the recommendation of party leaders representing 67 MKs; deadline 20 December 2026 with extension; new Knesset sworn in 10 November.
Netanyahu and his cabinet remain in office as a caretaker with limited powers until a new coalition forms; if Eisenkot fails Netanyahu could get a chance; failing that, elections in early spring.

Netanyahu formally requested a pardon in November 2025 without admitting guilt; on 26 April 2026 Herzog declined to rule and pushed for plea-deal talks with the Attorney General; Trump pressed Herzog to pardon him; the trial on bribery, fraud and breach of trust began in 2020.

claims.text: Israel has not signed the NPT and neither confirms nor denies having nuclear weapons; estimates of 80 to 400 warheads; Dimona built with French help in the 1950s; Vanunu revealed the programme in 1986.

ICJ, South Africa v. Israel: Israel filed its Counter-Memorial in March 2026, objecting to jurisdiction; an ICJ order of 21 May 2026 set South Africa's Reply for 22 November 2027 and Israel's Rejoinder for 22 May 2029; provisional-measures orders remain binding.

ICC Appeals Chamber, 24 April 2025: the arrest warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant "remain valid and unaffected by the jurisdictional review"; Israel's jurisdiction challenge was remitted to the Pre-Trial Chamber.

claims.text: On 8 February 2026 the security cabinet, on proposals by Smotrich and Defence Minister Israel Katz, approved: opening the West Bank land registry; repealing the Jordanian-era ban on land sales to non-Arabs and the transaction-permit requirement; moving planning authority for the Hebron settlement and the Cave of the Patriarchs, and control of Rachel's Tomb, to Israeli bodies; extending enforcement against Palestinian construction into Area A on heritage and archaeological grounds; reviving a committee for proactive land purchases. Smotrich's office: "we will continue to bury the idea of a Palestinian state." Security officials opposed the Hebron measures. Abbas called it dangerous; Jordan condemned it; Peace Now called it a path to a "massive land grab"; Regavim praised it.
